method: Conservative systematic ceiling: upper bounds on N-body contributions

shklovskii.conclusion: Shklovskii effect INCREASES Ṗ, cannot explain observed suppression. If anything, it makes the discrepancy worse by ~0.15 dex.
shklovskii.relevance: OPPOSITE to required direction - EXCLUDED as explanation

mass_segregation.mechanism: Mass segregation (spatial bias in observed population)
mass_segregation.direction: Could INCREASE mean Ṗ if biased to center
assumptions: Extreme segregation: only innermost 10% of pulsars observed
All outer pulsars completely missed (unrealistic given surveys)
mass_segregation.conclusion: Even with extreme assumptions, segregation contributes < 0.10 dex
mass_segregation.relevance: INSUFFICIENT: Explains at most 22% of observed suppression

binary_acceleration.direction: Could go either way depending on orbital phase
assumptions: All binary orbits have unmodeled systematic acceleration
Systematic direction aligned to explain suppression (unlikely)
binary_acceleration.relevance: NEGLIGIBLE: Explains at most 11% of observed suppression

selection_effects.conclusion: Selection effects INCREASE apparent Ṗ, cannot explain suppression
selection_effects.relevance: OPPOSITE to required direction - EXCLUDED as explanation

assumptions: Extreme metallicity gradient effect on Ṗ
metallicity.relevance: SMALL: Explains at most 18% of observed suppression

comparison.verdict: Maximum systematic (0.23 dex) explains only 65% of observed suppression (0.36 dex). Remaining 0.13 dex (1.6σ) requires non-systematic explanation.

assumptions_note: All bounds are CONSERVATIVE (generous to N-body explanation)
